lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Ah, hello again! I spent half the night on a hilltop gazing at the <color=red>constellations</color>, and I've only just found my way back.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: The stars inspired three <color=red>riddles</color>. Solve them all, and three new books will be delivered to the library.

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 1: I'm Earth's only natural <color=red>satellite</color>. My surface is scarred with craters, and my pull on the oceans creates the tides. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these travels around the Earth?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 2: I'm a planet named after a god of war, and my rusty, iron-rich dust gives me a <color=red>distinctive</color> red hue. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which planet is often called the Red Planet?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Riddle 3: I'm a frozen chunk of ice and dust on a long, <color=red>elliptical</color> orbit. As I approach the sun, I grow a glowing tail. What am I?
lines.hint: Not quite. Which of these is small, icy and known for its tail?

lines.speaker: Old Barnaby
lines.text: Splendid! Your <color=red>deductions</color> were flawless. Three new books are making their way to the library.

afterLines.speaker: Old Barnaby
afterLines.text: If you find yourself awake on a clear night, look up. The <color=red>cosmos</color> is far grander than any of my riddles.
